title: Compute a planar arm pose
scope: Planar 2R pose, not spatial FK, Jacobian or hardware

items.prompt: A tabletop pick-and-place arm must line its gripper up over a part lying on the table. Planar 2R arm: l1 = 1.25 m, l2 = 0.6 m; relative joint angles q1 = 0.5 rad, q2 = -0.5 rad (counter-clockwise positive; q1 is measured from the base +x axis, q2 from link 1). Compute the tip position x, y and the tool orientation theta (the world angle of link 2) modulo 2π. Tolerance ±0.001 m for x, y and ±0.001 rad for theta. You may leave theta unwrapped; if you reduce it, use 2π ≈ 6.2832. Keep at least 4 decimals in intermediate cos/sin values.
items.solution: Elbow: (l1 cos q1, l1 sin q1) = (1.25 cos 0.5, 1.25 sin 0.5) = (1.096978, 0.599282) m. Link 2 points at the world angle q1 + q2 = 0.5 + (-0.5) = 0 rad, so it adds (l2 cos(q1 + q2), l2 sin(q1 + q2)) = (0.6, 0) m. Tip: x = 1.096978 + 0.6 = 1.696978 m; y = 0.599282 + 0 = 0.599282 m. theta = q1 + q2 = 0 rad (any angle differing by a multiple of 2π is accepted).
hints: The joints are relative: link 1 points at q1 = 0.5 rad from the base +x axis, and link 2 points at the world angle q1 + q2, not at q2 = -0.5 rad alone. q2 is negative, so the elbow bends clockwise relative to link 1. Keep the calculator in radian mode.

Return the complete 3×3 homogeneous transform T_BT (maps tool coordinates into base coordinates), row by row, with the tool frame rotated by q1+q2; the translation entries are in metres.
